name: pgvector
model: Postgres extension: vector, halfvec, sparsevec and bit column types plus distance operators, used from plain SQL
engine_note: Index types HNSW and IVFFlat stored as Postgres index pages (shared buffers, WAL); data lives in normal Postgres heap tables on local disk
consistency: Inherits Postgres: multi-row ACID transactions, read committed by default, serializable as an option, fsync on commit by default. Approximate indexes filter after the scan, so filtered queries can return fewer rows unless iterative scans are on.
scaling: Same as the Postgres it runs in: bigger machine and read replicas; HNSW works best when the index fits in memory; sharding only via Citus or similar.
version_note: HNSW index added in 0.5.0 (2023-08-28); halfvec in 0.7.0 (2024-04-29); iterative index scans in 0.8.0 (2024-10-30).
reach: Reach for it when you already run Postgres and have up to tens of millions of embeddings to join, filter and delete in the same transaction as their rows.
avoid: Avoid at hundreds of millions to billions of vectors, or when index memory would crowd out the rest of your Postgres workload.
escape: It is the Postgres default for vectors; you leave it when vector count or recall/latency needs outgrow one Postgres.
chat: message_embeddings table next to messages; one SQL query does semantic search filtered by user_id.
notes: Latest 0.8.7 (2026-10-01) per CHANGELOG. Verified: HNSW exists (CHANGELOG 0.5.0: 'Added HNSW index type'); iterative index scans exist (0.8.0 (2024-10-30): 'Added support for iterative index scans'). Verified max indexed dimensions, README: 'vector - up to 2,000 dimensions', 'halfvec - up to 4,000 dimensions', 'bit - up to 64,000 dimensions'; FAQ: 'You can use half-precision vectors or half-precision indexing to index up to 4,000 dimensions or binary quantization to index up to 64,000 dimensions.' Filtering quote: 'With approximate indexes, filtering is applied *after* the index is scanned.' and 'Starting with 0.8.0, you can enable iterative index scans, which will automatically scan more of the index until enough results are found'. The stored (unindexed) vector type allows up to 16,000 dimensions per README (not re-quoted). Managed list: pgvector README has a hosted-Postgres list; specific providers named from their own pgvector support, not each re-fetched.
